This time, I want specific individual boroughs (not an overall city-wide pattern) that fall into one of these two categories:
- HOT SPOT: a borough with a high NO2 air pollution that is ALSO surrounded by other high-NO2 air pollution neighboring boroughs
- COLD SPOT: a borough with a low NO2 air pollution that is ALSO surrounded by other low-NO2 air pollution neighboring boroughs

Look at each borough together with its neighbors from the adjacency list, and identify any that qualify. Explain your reasoning, including a computed value for each borough you name. Note: dedicated spatial-statistics packages (pysal, esda, libpysal, geopandas, or similar) are NOT installed in this environment -- don't spend turns trying different import paths for them. For implementation including statistical method such as Moran's I, directly use only pandas and numpy. If you test statistical significance via a permutation/randomization test, use at least 500 random shuffles -- fewer permutations can produce an unstable p-value that lands on the wrong side of the 0.05 threshold just by chance, especially when the true effect is only moderate.

Thought: Now that I have the cleaned NO2 data and the adjacency mapping, I will calculate the average NO2 value for each borough and its neighbors. This will help me determine which boroughs qualify as hot spots (high NO2 surrounded by high NO2) and cold spots (low NO2 surrounded by low NO2). I will define thresholds for high and low NO2 values based on the overall distribution of the NO2 values.

Action:
```python
# Calculate the mean NO2 value to determine thresholds for high and low pollution
mean_no2 = df_no2_clean['value'].mean()
std_no2 = df_no2_clean['value'].std()

# Define thresholds for high and low NO2 values
high_threshold = mean_no2 + std_no2
low_threshold = mean_no2 - std_no2

# Identify hot spots and cold spots
hot_spots = []
cold_spots = []

for borough, neighbors in borough_neighbors.items():
    borough_value = df_no2_clean.loc[df_no2_clean['borough'] == borough, 'value'].values[0]
    
    # Get neighbor values
    neighbor_values = df_no2_clean.loc[df_no2_clean['borough'].isin(neighbors), 'value'].values
    
    # Check if the borough and its neighbors are above or below the thresholds
    if borough_value > high_threshold and all(neighbor_value > high_threshold for neighbor_value in neighbor_values):
        hot_spots.append((borough, borough_value))
    elif borough_value < low_threshold and all(neighbor_value < low_threshold for neighbor_value in neighbor_values):
        cold_spots.append((borough, borough_value))

# Display the thresholds and identified hot spots and cold spots
print("Mean NO2 Value:", mean_no2)
print("High Threshold:", high_threshold)
print("Low Threshold:", low_threshold)
print("Hot Spots:", hot_spots)
print("Cold Spots:", cold_spots)
```
